review:
If James Bond and Michael Bay had a baby...

and then that baby and Grand Theft Auto had a baby...

and then that baby and every 80s action movie had a baby...

that is this game.

Great game to waste time on from driving around, blowing shit up and collecting things. Though extremely repetitive, this has kept me entertained for 90+ hours. (and over 150+ hours on the free multiplayer mod)

[b]PROS[/b]
+ HUGE world map; we're talking 400 sq. miles (20 miles x 20 miles)
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=560068093
+ Great graphics (esp for 2010) that still hold up a half-decade later
+ Most PC's can easily handle this; a $100 GPU will max it out at 60 fps
+ Lots of mods available 
+ JC2MP, which adds much more things to do (and is free / 30mb)
+ Blowing up shit is fun
+ Lots of vehicles to utilize 
+ Perfect Draw Distance; you will always see the entire world! 
+ Nice weather system
+ One of the best Sandbox games out there
+ Affordable; 15$ normally; 2~5$ on sale

[b]CONS[/b]
- Extremely repetitive; you're basically just blowing up stuff for most of the game
- Dialogue / Missions are cheesy / bad
- World is far from ugly / barren, but there's few secrets / interesting points of interest
- Driving isn't the best
- Combat can get out of hand fast
- Little to do outside chaotic acts

This game will run very well on most computers as long as they have some power. If you can play CSGO at all you can play this. I have a lower mid-range PC (GTX 750 Ti / crappy old 3.0 Quad core AMD) and I have this maxed out at 60 fps at 1080p

If you love sandbox games this is a must-have, especially if it goes on sale. 

Overall, a B+ ~ A- game; it's a must-have for any sandbox fan.

This game is honestly the best in the series. I love how much content there is to enjoy. When it came out, I did buy just cause 3, but it seemed like the devs didn't put the same amount of love into that game. Within Just Cause 2, every little city or settlement across the mid-size landscape gave another little secret to enjoy. There was always something new to love. In just cause 3, the game mechanics and graphics are definitely the selling point, and they are beautifully made. However, after completing the campaign and a small handful of random races across the map, it's all that's left to enjoy. In just cause 2, there is so much added to it, including the faction missions, the agency missions, and the chaos unlock system, that even as someone whos completed most of the game, there is still things that you learn about it every time you play. The only interesting thing in jc3 is the crashed Mile High Club, which, btw is actually something in jc2 that is fully interactable and really awesome to play on. At a mere $15, along with the frequent sales, this game is a must-have for anyone's steam library.
Great open world game, amazing graphics, fun for anyone who likes to go out of their way and be creative with free roam, causing chaos and exploring.

Just Cause 2 gives you a massive island nation to freely explore, wreaking havok as you slowly discover hundreds of locations and find over a thousand items. JC2 is so insanely fun because it completely indulges the player while minimizing the tedious elements of open world games.

Other open world games require slow walking, but JC2 gives you over 50 vehicles (cars, tanks, fighter jets, and more) plus your essential grappling hook and parachute. If you’re hoofing it, you’re doing it wrong. Rather, open up the anywhere-accessible black market and buy a helicopter with dual-machine guns.

JC2’s biggest achievement is how it makes you feel totally in control, able to go anywhere and do anything. There are no invisible walls or disconnected “levels”. And visually, JC2 is really, really attractive. The weather and water are standouts still looking good years after release. The artwork is all very well-crafted, with amazing attention to detail.

The story is fun, too, with a very B-movie feel, intentionally hokey, but it works very well because of very solid voice work. The game also has a great self-awareness, featuring a hilarious dictator who will make you chuckle as he spouts his pontifications from loud speakers.

Are there downsides? A few. You run out of ammo often, but after 5 hours or so you learn to simply order new guns. There’s no stealth elements but that’s ok. Very few buildings have accessible interiors but no biggie. 

Overall, the large scope, consistent quality, and accessible controls of JC2 make it one of the purest video games ever created. When you’re tired of “serious” games let JC2 cleanse your gaming palette.

PC Players: The only Graphics option you need to turn off is "Decals" - otherwise it WILL CRASH whenever you shoot a bunch of stuff!!! Once you do that, you can let it run for days usually, hehe. It alt-tabs out fine, I usually have it running in the background all the time.

Good times, probably my favorite way to waste time. Yeah, I have a LOT of time to waste. BTW, the challenges are a count UP, not a count DOWN, so all the people with low times are cheaters! ;)

I like to use a Playstation 4 controller for motorcycles, planes and cars if I'm going a good distance and use the keyboard/mouse for everything else. CDPR should have hired this game's devs to create  a great driving environment for CyberPunk 2077, hahahaa!

[h1]REVIEW[/h1]
[i]Blow up a small fishing village's water tower in order to save their country. Why? Just 'cause.[/i]

[b]Just Cause 2[/b] is one of the best games around for exciting open-world mayhem. Nice graphics and animations, a diverse gameworld, and an interesting atmosphere establish an enjoyable explorative experience. The world is loaded with collectibles to find, vehicles to commandeer, and things to blow up. And it is headlined with exciting, distinctive gameplay chock-full of mayhem and destruction. If you are into sandbox mayhem, this should be a sure thing for you; and even more casual fans of the genre should easily enjoy this game too, because it is just so outright fun.

Now [b]Just Cause 2[/b], as is apparent by the title, is the sequel to the first [i]Just Cause[/i] game. The first game was decent, and I had some fun playing it. But to be honest: anything it can do, this can do better. Both games use the same core concepts for gameplay, except the ideas were certainly executed better in [b]Just Cause 2[/b]. So you really don’t have to worry too much about missing anything worthwhile if you would prefer skipping over the first game entirely. Even the narrative of [b]Just Cause 2[/b] is almost entirely unconnected to the first game’s story, so reading a brief synopsis should be more than sufficient for you to fully enjoy the experience. Having said all of that, though, if you really enjoy the genre, then you may want to check out the first game too. 

Anyway, the strongest attribute of [b]Just Cause 2[/b] has to be the riotous gameplay. You move around in an over-the-shoulder view while on foot, with various firearms at your disposal for taking out militants. And the patented grappling-hook mechanic allows some innovative ways to take down foes, bringing a distinctive novelty to the combat. Furthermore, shortly into the campaign, a wide variety of vehicles (cars, boats, helicopters, planes, and more) becomes available. These are great not only for your basic traveling needs, but also to perform ridiculous and hilarious stunts. And of course, the grappling-hook and parachute combination can be used to explore the gameworld in the signature [i]Just Cause[/i] fashion that affords the franchise its unique identity. And with the myriad of collectibles to find, structures to destroy, statistics to record, and achievements to unlock: there is no shortage of things to do.

And I suppose if the gameplay is the best attribute of the game, then the gameworld presentation is a very close second. The graphics are pristine and the landscape is packed with diverse sceneries and environments. From mountain peaks to desert valleys, it has it all. The animations and effects are also mostly well designed, which enhances the gratification of bringing a wake of destruction through every last place you visit. And the world is humongous. Even with a jet it can take a while to cross the map. Luckily there is a fast travel system that allows you to begin a sky-dive from above any location you have visited. It integrates perfectly with the game, taking what would be tedious and flipping it into one of the most enjoyable things to do. [b]Just Cause 2[/b] easily has one of the most entertaining gameworlds to explore.

But even with all of this going on, the game starts off with a very focused and linear mission that allows you to be introduced to the main narrative elements of the campaign. You will come to find, however, that the story aspects of [b]Just Cause 2[/b] are minimal, and mostly mediocre. So you definitely shouldn’t go into it expecting to be told an elaborate story. But despite that, the narrative flows and the various missions are certainly enjoyable. The missions are purposeful and focused, which can be a refreshingly stark contrast to the mindless mayhem side of the game. But while there is a decent amount of total missions including the extras, there are very few main storyline missions, which does hold the overall experience back a bit. So there is some room for improvement.

Ultimately, [b]Just Cause 2[/b] is a good example of what can be done in video games when great concepts meet great execution. It is such an all-around fun and distinctive experience that I would recommend everyone give it some consideration; and if you are a fan of the genre, then it should be a no-brainer.

And as an addendum: there is now a free multiplayer mod DLC. With the mod, the opportunity for hilarious stunts and mayhem is increased exponentially as numerous players can all play in the same sandbox at once. As a free bonus, it is a pretty sweet addition and can be a lot of fun if you like that kind of thing. Luckily, if it doesn’t sound like your thing, it is also easy to completely ignore since the mod installs as a separate “app” on Steam with separate statistics and achievements tracking.

[h2]In-depth[/h2] 
[h3]⚔️ Gameplay & Exploration: [/h3]  

Just Cause 2 is an open-world action-adventure game where you play as Rico Rodriguez, a special American agent tasked to hold control over the Panau islands by liberating them islands. You do this in the good old American fashion, blowing up everything that stands in your way, creating chaos, and controlling each point on the map.

The gameplay is divided into a few things. taking control over villages, bases, airports, and other areas of interest, doing side-missions for your 3 allies that each try to take control of the map, killing important enemy leaders and playing with different vehicles, collecting items, and exploring the vast and complex islands.

The islands are gorgeous, despite the fact that this game came a decade ago. It still holds up very well the visuals and the physics are fairly good too, making it feel like a rather good game to play.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3168185487

[h3]😄 Fun: [/h3]

It really depends on what side of the barrel are you looking at from. If you're here to beat the story, it's a better and fun experience to have. If you're here to complete, then you better look elsewhere, because this game doesn't value your time, enjoyment, or patience.

[h3]🏞 Visuals & Presentation: [/h3]  

Great looking game for its age. I normally look for mods for games that are fairly old to feel a bit better while playing, but to be honest, I didn't feel I needed this game. I think you'll find a lot of stunning views, impressive achievements made by the developers, and a lot of love put in the world.

The cinematics are trying to portray a James Bond feel to it, and it nails it in some parts.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2855777188

[h3]🔊 Sound & Voice-Acting: [/h3]  

The music is the weakest part of this game. It's non-existent in vehicles and very repetitive in the world. Something I wish the game did better.

Dialogues and voice-acting is not that impressive either, even for the main characters. It felt a bit forced and lifeless.

[h3]📖 Story & Writing: [/h3]  

The story revolves around Rico discovering the secrets behind Panau Islands, as he and his team try to take a special role in liberating, infiltrating and taking down the leaders of Panau one by one. New and old characters are introduced in the story, with some interesting events.

I did like the James Bond feel of the story, but it was rather dull from transitioning from Cinematics to the game and such. It was hard to find the characters believable in some parts.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3171155376

[h3]🧵 Length & Difficulty: [/h3]  

It's a humongous game to explore. One of the largest maps I've ever played. I didn't think anything could beat Ubisoft, but it seems to me it did. It's a large and lengthy game. Although you can beat it a lot sooner, you're required to gather chaos, by destroying as much as possible in order to progress.

It's not a difficult game to complete, but it's very mundane and tedious, making it more of a drag than anything else.

[h3]⭕️Verdict: [/h3]  
Just Cause 2 is a great improvement overall over the first game, with stunning visuals, impressive physics, fun mechanics, and a gorgeous world to explore. Although it's not perfect, it's a fun game to blow steam, play at your own pace, and dive into the world that has much to show and tell you.

Open-world action game as it should be. [b]Just Cause 2[/b] has that great feeling of absolute freedom - go anywhere, drive anywhere, fly anywhere! You can get to any place on the huge map in just few seconds, you can be defeated without any penalties - this game is here to entertain you, not to blow your mind or make you angry at your keyboard.

Two unique devices underlying the awesomeness of [b]Just Cause 2[/b] are grappling hook and infinitely respawning parachute (infinitely resp...? aw, forget it). Tons of fun guaranteed! Every action game should have it - I really missed them in [b]Far Cry 3[/b]. ;-) It brings so much variety and joy in moving and fighting that you'll be travelling for hours here and there just to use them again and again.

The world is really good. Yes, most of the cities and villages are copy-pasted, but there are so many different regions on the map with different climate, weather and views that you'll never get bored. Graphics is on the level too, especially fire and explosions - you'll get addicted to blowing things up! Story and quests are not the strongest part of the game, but they do their job. Another feature worth mentioning is the hidden items' search radar - in my opinion, really great idea. It is finally interesting to find stuff by yourself without spending hours in vain or using guide from the Internet.

There are some cons, of course. Enemies respawning out of nowhere behind your back can be really annoying sometimes. Weapon arsenal is not so big, besides, the lack of ammunition for some weapons leaves you with even less choices. Main story is very short and optional quest lines are not so long either. But there are many things to do on the map - different challenges, races, liquidation contracts... Finally, there's still (and I guess it will be there forever) a bug that prevents you from getting the cherished 100% completion of the game (by the game's internal statistics, not the Steam's one). Thankfully there's only achievement for 75% completion, so no worries, achievement hunters - you'll get your perfect Steam game. ;-)

If you like free roaming in beautiful open-world game, spending time in parachute challenges, races and outpost fightings, searching for hundreds of collectibles and upgrades, spreading chaos by blowing stuff up or just flying around and enjoing you freedom - you'll definitely love [b]Just Cause 2[/b].

------------------------------

Экшн с открытым миром - такой, каким он должен быть. [b]Just Cause 2[/b] дарит чувство абсолютной свободы - иди куда хочешь, рули куда хочешь, лети куда заблагорассудится. В любую точку огромной карты можно добраться за секунды, никаких штрафов за гибель героя - эта игра призвана развлекать вас, а не взрывать мозг или доводить до бешенства.

Два уникальных девайса, делающих игру такой шикарной - гарпун и бесконечно восстанавливающийся парашют (бесконечно восстан...? а, неважно). Веселье гарантировано! Эти штуки должны быть в каждом экшене - как мне не доставало их в [b]Far Cry 3[/b]!.. ;-) Простое перемещение по миру и заурядные перестрелки становятся настолько разнообразней и веселей, что вы будете путешествовать туда-сюда только для того, чтобы снова воспользоваться ими.

Мир игры по-настоящему хорош. Да, большая часть городков и деревень сделана копи-пастом. Но на карте столько разных мест со своим климатом, погодой, видами вокруг, что скучно не будет. Графика тоже на уровне, особенно огонь и взрывы - вы полюбите разносить всё в щепки! Сюжет и побочные квесты не сильная сторона игры, но своё дело они делают. Отдельного упоминания стоит система поиска скрытых предметов с помощью радара - на мой взгляд, отличное решение! В кои-то веки интересно искать ценные предметы самому, а не бегать часами там, где ничего нет, или сверяться с готовой картой из Инета.

Конечно, есть некоторые минусы. Враги, респавнящиеся из ниоткуда прямо за спиной, порой жутко раздражают. Арсенал не так уж велик, а нехватка патронов для некоторых пушек ещё сильнее ограничивает в выборе. Основная сюжетная линия очень коротка, да и дополнительные квесты проходятся быстро. Тем не менее, заняться есть чем - всяких испытаний, гонок и контрактов на устранение на карте хватает. Наконец, достичь заветного 100%-го прохождения игры (игра ведёт свою внутреннюю статистику, не связаную со Steam) не получится из-за бага, который, очевидно, никто уже не исправит. К счастью, Steam-достижение есть только за 75%-ое прохождение, так что будьте спокойны, охотники за ачивами - вы сможете получить в коллекцию ещё одну "идеальную" игру. ;-)

Если вам нравится рассекать по открытому красивому миру, проводить время за парашютными испытаниями, гонками и сражениями за военные базы, искать сотни спрятанных предметов и апгрейдов, сеять хаос, взрывая всё вокруг, или просто летать, наслаждаясь видом и собственной свободой, вам определённо понравится [b]Just Cause 2[/b].

Just Cause 2 is a legendary over the shoulder sandbox shooter along the lines of Grand Theft Auto without the charm. The game focuses on destruction, deep controls and doing whatever craziness you'd like to do. You play as Rico Rodriguez and you've been sent in by the government to mess things up like a kitten in tissue paper on an island nation that seems giant by gaming standards. You have the option work for different factions / gangs that have their own agendas. The gangs are a nice touch and you'll see them battle each other on the island while civilians run and hide. It's a nice AI dichotomy.

Since the game is set on a bunch of giant islands, the terrain is gorgeous and diverse. You'll see lush green jungles beneath icy mountains, then go into those icy mountains and down into sandy deserts. After that, you can take a boat for a ride across beautiful blue waters, then hijack a jet and surf on top of it into a golden sunset while dodging missiles. Everywhere in this game is a gorgeous place and there are tons of places to visit and blow up. There doesn't seem to be any interiors, but that is fitting for a game so beautiful with good traversal diversity.

The controls are deep, but they allow you to do a lot more than your average over the shoulder sandbox shooter. You have your standard, run, jump, gunfire, reload, grenade, toggle guns, toggle grenades buttons, but you also have the infamous grapple hook. This hook is what the Bionic Commando reboot was missing. A simple press will send you instantly zipping to wherever it latched onto. Traversal is made super easy, climbing up buildings with the hook, but you have a parachute that is used to glide around or launch yourself in combination with the grappler. Simply hit the jump button while in the air to deploy the chute. Pressing and holding the grappling hook will grapple something, but then when you hold it, aim at something else and release the button, you've now tethered two things together, which results in hilarity. Tether a moving car to the ground, to watch the car flip over. Tether a NPC to a rocketing propane tank and watch them blast off. There is plenty of car combat. Normal games would have you just get in a car, but in Just Cause 2, you can get on top of the car to shoot things, or you can slip down in front or behind the car to shoot things using the car for cover as it's moving. If there's no driver and you're vehicle surfing, you have a bit of control over the vehicle. You can take over moving vehicles, with easy quick time events that show a struggle instead of just kicking a person out from behind the wheel.

Combat is pretty easy, you just aim the cursor and fire. There is no aim button, if your cursor is remotely near anyone or anything, you will see a red highlight around the logical target. So if you the player have terrible aim, Rico Rodriguez will still shoot the target. In terms of holding guns, you can hold one two handed gun and two one handed guns. There are throwable explosives and you can toggle between two types. You can also melee enemies with the grappling hook.

With so much control freedom, you can tackle missions any way that you want. Such as a car chase mission where you need to escort the driver, do you grappling hook vehicle to vehicle, taking out enemies and struggling to knock out the driver? Do you tether the other vehicles to the ground and watch them crash, or do you use your parachute to hover over the action and blow up the other vehicles? Even a simple beat the clock race that forces you to have a land vehicle... well I could use that fancy red car over there, but I'm already driving a tank, so I'll take the tank. The choice is yours. It is an excellent game to do what you want.

Missions themselves give you easy to follow objectives as if they were steps to follow. Open the gate, take out that rocket launcher, take out those snipers, pick up that item, grapple onto that helicopter, and so on. The objectives are marked with red and easily found with how far away they are. If you try to deviate too far from a mission location, the game will warn you and start a 10 second counter. This keeps the intensity on and prevents people like me from exploiting things.

Outside of missions, there are plenty of things to do and they're all marked on your map. Well you need to visit the location marked on your map before you find what it is there to do. Things such as races, time trials, destroy bases and loot villages. Destroying locations and looting villages each has a percentage attached to it. To loot a village, you need to find 100% of things hidden there. Things like vehicle parts, weapon parts, cash boxes and even liberate the village from propaganda buses. Thankfully when you get near something collectable, it will show up pointing out where you are, but you need to be very near it. This saves you from detailed searching. It is the same for ammo boxes and health cabinets.

As for the bases, you need to find things and blow up things such as towers, generators, gas tanks, communication towers and surface-to-air missile launchers, each will make up 100%. It is fun for explorers to seek out every nook and cranny, but I can understand if getting 100% would feel like a chore.

When you create chaos or break any sort of law, the local military will be sent after you. At first it'll be simple things hunting you down, but if you keep creating chaos, your 'heat' level will go up and more soldiers will come after you. How do you reduce your heat level? Hide. Yep hide in the jungle and after time your red heat will go to orange heat and start dropping down. This is good for keeping the focus on what you were doing before you created heat. With plenty of jungle in the game, it is pretty easy to ditch any heat you might have.

Sadly the enemies feel pretty dumb. No one takes cover when you're putting bullets into them, even if enemies are next to cover, but I guess people play for the fun of doing what they want, rather than the challenge. In car chases enemy vehicles will just ram other objects. It leads to some laughable moment. They'll just drive off cliffs when you hit the brakes. I can understand scripted events like running into a gas station, but otherwise it is hilariously bad.

The game is pretty easy even on normal with regenerating health. There are also health pickups from cabinets seem well placed. If you die, you go to the last checkpoint during a mission. Sometimes the checkpoints are further back than you think, but that's the only thing that really presents a punishment in the game.

The real downside to the game is that it seems to crash once every few hours back to the desktop. This seems to be caused by having decals on in the video settings and another setting, so turning them off prevents the crash. Luckily the game has an autosave feature.

To top all of that off, there is a free Multiplayer MOD that allows every player into one world together for chaos to ensue. Is it worth $15? Sure.... but it has been on sale before at $2.50. Keep that in mind.

[h1]How I Found Out About "Just Cause 2"[/h1]
The same way I found out about a lot of games, from YouTube. I randomly came across a video that was showing someone driving a vehicle off of a tall snowy mountain. The crash and destruction effects made me fall in love. See, I've always loved destruction in games/movies/etc. So when I see something like that, I know I must own the game. 

[h1]Unfair First Impressions[/h1]
I've seen a lot of different unfair first impressions for this game. The first, and most simple being, the fact that someone may not have liked the original Just Cause game. Therefor it leads to an automatic thought that any sequel will be just as bad, or worse. I can understand this, but believe me, Just Cause 2 makes everything better. 

Second, I've heard that the game can get low reviews and less players because of it's story. I know some people are looking for games for their story. However, not everyone is. You can have a game like Just Cause 2 where the story is bad but the gameplay is good, very good. 

Third, because it's a [b]third person shooter[/b] style of game. Which can turn some people away. 

[h1]Review Of "Just Cause 2"[/h1]
Just Cause 2 is a massive [b]open world[/b], [b]sandbox[/b], [b]TPS[/b] game, that comes with a full story, side missions, bonus missions, and so many collectables that you'll die before finding all of them. 

The world of Just Cause 2 is massive (Panau). One of biggest I have ever seen! Stretching across desert terrain and mountains, snowy mountains and terrain, jungle and marsh, ocean, urban areas, and military bases. One downside to the world of Just Cause 2 is that it may be very big, but it's not well populated with stuff. Meaning, all that jungle and desert, 90% of it will not have anything in it besides sand and trees. So you may find the world itself being very boring at times. However, the rest of the game makes up for that. In the world of Just Cause 2, there are urban areas to explore. Villages that may hold resources and ammo to big cities that contain higher costing vehicles & helicopters. Places like airports where you can obtain a passenger jet. There are military bases you can liberate by destroying & collecting all things within it. These bases could consist of ports, vehicle factories, little infantry camps, to big fortress type places. 

You can get around the world of Just Cause 2 with many things. First of all, you can use your [b]grappling hook[/b] to get to higher places, then you can use your [b]parachute[/b] to glide down or travel across land faster. Not only is that the most basic of travel, there are vehicles...a lot. There are a little over 100 vehicles in Just Cause 2. Anything from ATV's, motorcycles, cars, trucks, boats, armored cars, planes, helicopters, etc. The list goes on. One thing that I do not care for in the vehicle department is the vehicle physics. The vehicle isn't really that responsive, or reliable. You can hit the movement key lightly and the vehicle will spin out, even at low speeds. 

You can defend yourself with weapons like SMG's, shotguns, etc. There really aren't many weapons to use in the default game unless you purchase DLC. However, there is still so much content in the game, you don't actually need DLC so the DLC is just there for bonus weapons & vehicles. I would like it if Just Cause 2 had more weapons in the default game. With how big the world is, having more weapons gives you more options to do things with.

This isn't really the game that plays like a TPS game. You don't run up to a base and get behind cover then start attacking. The AI is kind of stupid, and the same time, they work well. There really isn't any stealth. The concept behind Just Cause 2 is that you drive in for fly in, kill everything, and walk away from a massive explosion. 

As for the story and side missions. The story itself is generic and not really exciting, except for the final mission. There are only six missions I believe, maybe more. However, to unlock story missions you must gain [b]chaos[/b] which can be obtained by destroying key points in military bases, fighting the military, collecting things, or completing side missions. There are a lot of side missions to choose from three different [b]sub factions[/b] who you'll find fighting the military at times. The side missions themselves can actually be unique and fun, however the briefing itself is low. Every mission start, you'll stand there and the leader of the sub faction will drive by, tell you what you need to do, and then drive away. Not a word said. 

Don't get me wrong, Just Cause 2 is a great game, it just may not be what you are looking for. 

[h1]Content In Just Cause 2 (Bonus Missions & Collectables)[/h1]
In the world of Just Cause 2, you have bonus missions alongside "side missions". These mainly consist of races, for all vehicle types. 

Other then that, you have thousands of collectables. These can be little pickups for the sub factions, or little resource crates that boost your stats, like giving you weapon parts to upgrade your weapons, or armor parts to give you more health, etc. 

To gain 100% in Just Cause 2 requires you to collect every piece of sub faction items and resources, also, destroying key military structures in an area. Each area you discover will give you a progress bar, when everything has been collected or destroyed, the progress bar will reach 100% and that area is clear. However, the PC version of Just Cause 2 experienced a bug where a few items & structures do not spawn in the game. Therefor it is impossible to beat the game 100% without a mod. The devs apparently do not care to fix this easily fixed problem. 

[h1]Pro's & Con's (Overall Rating)[/h1]
Just Cause 2 is an open world TPS that provides a wide variety of collectables and fun destruction. You can spend hours on the game before ever reaching 15% for full completion. Despite needing a mod to fully beat the game 100%. There has alos been a community mod released that allows people to play together in the world of Panau. 

Pro's:
+Massive open world.
+Loads of collectables for hours of game time.
+Fun destruction system.
+Addicting "I must find everything" style.
+DLC is not required to play.
+Nice variety of vehicles.

Con's:
-Mod needed for full completion.
-Enemy will spam helicopters.
-Mostly boring empty world. 
-Strange vehicle mechanics.
-Low leveled main story & side mission briefing.


Overall Rating: About A 12/15 (A Nice Game That's Worth A Pickup)

[h1] If you're looking for a detailed Just Cause 2 review then you're at the right place. [/h1]

[h1]Pros [/h1]
+Just Cause 2 is the very definition of how a sandbox game should be made. Avalanche Studios mastered the art of creating huge open world simulators that lead them to Just Cause 3, Mad Max, Rage 2 and even new IPs.
+At 400km sq. JC2 features one of the largest open world maps ever! Everything is highly detailed, and diverse. Also, there are no loading screens unless you want to fast travel or participate in missions. There's just so much to explore. From big cities to tropical islands, exotic beaches, sandy deserts, tall mountains, cold regions, dense forests and enemy bases. JC2 has it all! 
+Breathtaking explosions. Just Cause 2 is all about causing destruction and chaos. 
+Surprisingly a lot of hidden secrets and easter eggs. You gotta find them all!!
+Lots of graphical settings and options for PC users. Works on low spec PCs too which is nice if you're stuck with an office laptop. 
+Graphics look amazing considering it’s almost a decade old game. This is a massive improvement over the first game. Let’s be honest......no one really cares about the first game. 
+Just Cause 2 gives you complete freedom when it comes to completing missions. You'll be rewarded for being creative. 

[h1]Cons [/h1]
-The writing and plot will make you wonder if they hired a 12 year old to write the script. 
-Laughably bad voice acting, any line of dialogue should be enough to make you either laugh or cry. Cringe worthy performance. No words to describe how bad it really is. 
-Terrible checkpoint system. If you fail a mission or die, you are forced top complete the whole mission from the start which gets really frustrating after a few hours. You're out of luck if the game crashes to desktop to luckily there's an autosave feature.
-Buying weapons and upgrades is a tedious task because there's a loot drop cutscene every time you feel like buying something or just interested in fast travel. This is a problem with all side missions. 
-Driving is very clunky and doesn't hold up really well today. 
-Side missions get really tedious and repetitive after a few hours
-Whole cities feel empty. There are rarely any civilians and npcs throughout the game. They spawn and disappear right infront of you which is very disappointing especially when you're playing on a PC at max settings. Perhaps a limitation with the game engine. Enemies and vehicles also have a habit of respawning a lot
-Numerous bugs and glitches. A few times I had to restart the game because I got stuck in buildings and cars. That's totally expected from a game with such a large scale. 
-Crashed multiple times on my Windows 10 PC but that didn't stop me for playing over 80 hours! 

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
Easily the best looking game of 2010. I recommend this game to anyone who loves fun open world games and sandbox shooters. Just Cause 2 boasts a solid action-packed and impressive open world, however it's generic story and unrefined gunplay and driving mechanics cause the game to still unfortunately miss the mark that it could. That's just my personal opinion..... What do you think though? [b] I give Just Cause 2 a [b]7/10[/b]

Y'know, Just Cause 3 (Yes, I'm talking about 3 really quick, hear me out) had a much more refined game experience: the shooting controls were tighter, the grapple was far more versatile and useful, the parachute was easier to control, and the wingsuit was a blast to use and was a great addition to the game. The explosions were bigger, the voice acting was more tolerable, the weapons were crazier, and so on. I could list many more things that JC3 does better than JC2.

But you know what? Despite ALL of that, Just Cause 2 has a certain charm to it that 3 doesn't. JC2 is honestly just...I dunno. It's so much more fun to play. Maybe it's because it feels less generic and AAA-ish. Maybe it's because you didn't have to do little challenges and destroy the same boring props in every town to progress. Maybe it's because the world was more varied and interesting, and towns and bases felt like actual places instead of bullet points on a list of things to blow up. Just Cause 2, as unpolished as it is, ends up being the more enjoyable game in my opinion. And this is just vanilla; JC2 is stupidly easy to mod, and there's tons of crazy mods out there to really crank up the insanity. Naturally, it's also far easier to run than JC3. Even the craptop I keep in my room can handle this game at 30fps on low settings.

You get to keep Just Cause 2 [strike]forever[/strike] until Steam explodes.

Just Cause 2 is an example of when video games are trying to be just that, a video game. No gimmick, no microtransactions and no bull***, Just Cause 2 is a game pumped to the brim with steroids layered with bazillions things to do. And it still holds up really well with today's games, some areas it is even better than any game released in the couple of years. 

The Good:
+ Fun sandbox-style game that gives you the freedom to explore and do as you please right from the getgo. Like literally, there will be an introduction/tutorial mission in the beginning to teach you the basics but after that the game pretty much take the reins off you and let you roam freely
+ Hours of gameplay content, ranging from basic missions to progress the story to side activities like racing. The game also gives you a lot of toys to play with, which you can unlock more the further you progress in the game
+ Freedom to approach missions as you see fit. You can attempt to infiltrate a military base either guns blazing, using an attack helicopter or be crazy and become the crazy saboteur always dream of, wielding bazookas and tons of grenades
+ B-Movie hilarity. While other action games in this similar genre tries to be serious, Just Cause 2 knows that it is an action B-Movie type game and have fun with itself. From the crazy things you can do on this game, like jumping out of a helicopter to another helicopter and the crazy boss battles you meet (there's a battle with a Chinese psychopath wielding fireworks lol), Just Cause 2 know that it's not trying to be a 'serious' game, and I loved it for that
+ The graphics and visuals for this game is really good for a game released back in 2009. Character models and textures does look outdated but the environment and looks spectacular

The Bad:
- Story is pretty much nonexistent. The basic plot in this game is that Rico Rodriguez, our main action hero has been given the task to be an undercover agent in Panau Island, trying to uncover a government conspiracy that may be a threat to Panau and its citizens. Although seem like a decent plot, it quickly become forgettable with boring cutscenes and uninteresting characters
- Driving controls for land vehicles (cars, motorbikes) are mostly terrible. They are difficult to steer and doesn't feel responsive. Sea and air vehicles however, handles really good and I used it more to travel more between places than using land vehicles
- Enemies are pretty much bullet sponges, they just keep respawning and respawning and most of time i feel like I am wasting my ammo on them
- The world feels empty at times. Even though this is an open world, it doesn't feel like a breathing one. 

The Verdict:
Just Cause 2 is an amazing game with lots of hours of things to do and plenty of mayhem to cause. It has some flaws, but the engaging and fun gameplay makes up for that. What other game lets you jump out of a helicopter into another helicopter and makes you look cool doing so?

To preface, please don't let my hours played fool you; I completed JC2 99.95% on PS3 back in the day, which remains the highest completion percentage you can achieve on that version. I still fire it up from time to time.

This review will be short; Just Cause 2 is an amazing game that was mindblowing upon release, but holds up to this day. A title polished to such a great extent that you'd be hardpressed to find a recent game that has received a similar amount of QA.

Unfortunately, JC2 is also the only game worth playing in the series. The original is now too archaic, and had its fair share of problesm; the third and fourth games however.... oh boy. Those two were made by a newly founded dev team in New York, and are of such technical marvel that you can only wonder whether it was stuck together with washi tape or bubble gum by a bunch of interns who flunked out of community college. 

Just Cause 3 was unplayable at launch, and remains a crippled game to this day through its locking of fun features behind dreadful time trials and other such challenges. Just Cause 4 had a similar nuclear holocaust of a launch, and strayed even further from JC2's perfection in its decision to do away with destruction altogether.

No, I can tell you this much, dear reader; if you see JC3 and JC4 on sale, and feel the itch to play them, then please, please resist the temptation, and get Just Cause 2. Yes, it's age is slowly starting to show, and no, it doesn't have quite as many brainless gimmicks as the later games, but it is actually competently made, and good, pure, simple fun, with no ifs or buts. GIven how cheap it is during every Steam sale, I dare say it is one of the few essential titles that should be in everyone's library.

Added bonus; it will run on any old toaster.

So, Just Cause 2 is a fun game with some problems.

You play as man called Rico. I wish I could tell you anything about him, but playing through the game twice and getting all achievements after 72 hours ingame, I didn't learn anything about anyone. Maybe you learn it all in Just Cause 1, but I haven't played that game.
The storyline however, is that you are on an Asian isle called Panau who is dictated by President Panay.
You go undercover and work for the three local gangs on the isle to make their leaders trust you enough to give you information on Panay that you can use to assassinate him.

+PROS+
+The world is COMPLETELY open! There are no limits to where you can go or any invisible walls.
+300 collectibles scattered around the island you can collect for the gangs.
+You are incredibly mobile, with your grappling hook and parachute on your back, there is nowhere you cannot get to.
+Many driving challenges that will test your skills on land, water and in the air.
+Very diverse world. You have tall snowy mountains, a giant desert, forests, a vast ocean, jungles and a huge city.
+A total of 49 missions you can do for the three gangs.
+You can kill enemies in really interesting ways if you use your imagination.
+Variety in areas. You will take over and liberate small villages, cities, military bases, oil rigs, airports and plenty more.
+Alot of vehicles you can use to transport yourself around. The base game has 104 vehicles, but with DLCs there are even more. Everything from small mopeds, monster trucks and tanks to giant jets and attack helicopters.
+EXPLOSIONS

-CONS-
-The main story is super short and it sucks.
-Alot of areas are copied and pasted. As an example, all oil rigs are built the exact same way, all the weak points are on the same places, and all the loot is located in the same places.
-Way too few weapons. I think without DLCs, there are 7 weapons you can choose from, and DLCs adds 5 or 6 more I think.
-I experienced a total of 3 random crashes, and it crashes 90% of the time when you try to exit the game.
-It gets repetitive very fast. When you go to areas who look more or less the same, fight enemies who all look and say the same with the exact same weapons and you destroy the same kind of stuff, you lose motivation fast.
-I really wish you could see some results of all you do. If you liberate enough villages and towns, there could be riots between the police and the civilians. When you take over an airport, there would sometimes be friendly choppers coming to help you. When you kill enough generals, the police would stop chasing you a little earlier than usual. But as it is, you can take over almost every single zone, and the army will have the exact same presence in the streets as they did when you started.

The game will soon be 8 years old. And while it does show its age, it has aged quite well.
If you are looking for a great story, or a story at all, look elsewhere. But if you want to blow up government property and kill their military forces, Panau is the place to go.

I remember the first time I played Just Cause 2.
It was early 2010. I was sixteen, my soul hungry for chaos, my heart still unaware of the weight nostalgia would one day carry.
That day, I bought a cheap copy with some leftover birthday money.
A plastic case, a simple disc, for my dusty old PC.
But it wasn’t just a game.
It was the beginning of something.
It was Just Cause 2.

I installed it, launched it, and it was as if the real world faded away.
I spent every hour of that day soaring across Panau.
The jungles, the cities, the deserts — stitched together by impossible stunts and explosions.
I wasn’t playing it. I was living it.

And then came so many freefalls, so many crazy escapes. Endless hours tethering enemies to gas tanks and sending them flying.
I knew every village, every military base, every hidden easter egg.
And without any guide—when YouTube tutorials were still slow and rare—I found every upgrade, every ridiculous secret.
It was my world.
It was home.

Every now and then, my father would glance at the screen, shaking his head at the madness.
He came from a world of Pac-Man and Space Invaders — a world with no parachutes, no grappling hooks.
I still remember the time I showed him how to skydive off a helicopter onto a moving car.
He just laughed and said, “That’s not a game. That’s a movie.”
It was my refuge.
It was our small bridge.

And now, years later, I go back.
The world has changed. I have changed. I’m thirty-one now.
And he... he’s no longer here.

Yet every time I boot up Just Cause 2, it feels like opening a window into the past.
The graphics are rougher now, the controls a bit stiff, but the heart remains untouched.
Every explosion, every whistling freefall, every ridiculous stunt speaks a language only the soul can hear.
It’s the voice of youth.
It’s the whisper of my father laughing at the impossible.

Just Cause 2 isn’t just a game.
It’s a time machine.
It’s a second chance to touch, even for a moment, what we thought we had lost.

And as I grapple onto a helicopter in the sunset skies of Panau, I remain there.
Fingers on the keyboard...
And a tear I cannot tell — whether it’s sorrow or gratitude.

Wow.....what a bloody blast!  This game has such a marvelous gameplay loop, that just keeps you coming back for more and more and more (up to a point....).

Positives:

-Graphics-  It's a little dated, and obviously there's a TON of repeated base, city, and village elements (you will get sick of taking out satellite transmission bases, dozens of the buggers, each with a destructible radio tower, generator, antenna activated after a three button activation, and a resource somewhere in the camp......EVERY single one), but the environments are varied, pretty to look at, and fun to navigate through.

-Gameplay-  You will blow up damned near everything, and earn money and Chaos points everytime you do so.  As well, there are colonels to be assassinated, three different types of faction collectibles, and four different varieties of resources (cash, health, weapon upgrade crates, and vehicle upgrade crates), and a bloody TON of villages and military bases to be liberated and/or destroyed.   You will NOT be bored (for the first 80 hours or so ;-)  ;-)

Meh:

-Writing/Dialogue/Plot-  Perfunctory at best and trite at worst.  The main storyline is utter tripe and the character dialogue stinks on ice (and you WILL get sick of hearing the protagonist's utterances over and over and over and over and over again, "That was fun!", "It's a dirty job, but someone's got to do it", etc etc etc).

Negatives:

-Bugs-  Turn off the decals or you will almost certainly be subjected to crash after crash after crash any time the action gets even moderately thick.  As well, you may occasionally find yourself stuck on objects or unable to do things like switch weapons, attack, fire your grappling hook, etc if you're too close to certain parts of the environment (there were several times where I couldn't attack a guy even though he was right beside me, shooting the heck outta me, because the game thought I was too close.......weird).

-Game size-  Look, the map that you will be exploring by grappling hook, on foot, boat, plane, helicopter, car, motorcycle, etc etc is roughly 35 km by 35 km, and there are over 350 places to visit, as well as all the collectibles scattered throughout the map.  Hard to believe I'm saying this, but the map is just too darned big and full of things to do.  I'm calling it quits now that I've beaten the main mission and completed 75% of the locations/collectibles.  It's just going to become too samey (in fact, it already kinda is), so I'm not going to cave in to my usual compulsion to 100% everything.

-Mission design-  Most are fine, but the final two missions (6 & 7) are linked back to back, and you really can't go do anything else once you start (you can, but it won't be saved if you die, and you'll go right back to the beginning of mission 7 if you try) and while you can obviously come back after in Mercenary Mode to finish whatever you didn't get done first, the game doesn't warn you of the railroading nature of the missions.  A little prompt that says something like, "If you accept Mission 6, you will have no choice but to finish it and Mission 7 back to back" would have let the player know whether they should screw around a bit more first in the game world before entering end-game.

Despite my kvetches, the overall game is a metric craptonne of fun!

Highly recommended!!!

Do you want to surf a 747? You can. Do you want to fly as high as possible and then just skydive for a nice 5 or 6 minutes? You can. Do you want to hijack a chopper mid-air and use it to destroy an oil refinery just for the thrill of it? You can. This is up there as one of the most fun sandbox games to date. 

Unfortunately, however, the world is pretty shallow, and for all the locations and collectibles, the breadth of the gameplay is fairly limited. It's not a living, breathing world like the GTA worlds - the environment (which looks wonderful and varied enough in terms of climate and locations) is inhabited by people without personalities, and who exist only to be shot at, blown up, or otherwise maimed. The missions are compelling to a degree, although there is a degree of repetition in the faction missions that would become grating if the action wasn't so fun. However, I didn't at any point on XBOX or PC find myself compelled to 100% the game, as this involves hours of repetition with little tangible reward. This is felt the most when the end-game is at hand, and there's not a lot to motivate you to play beyond the completion of the missions. 

The story isn't very compelling or coherent, but it is bad to the point of *almost* coming around to good again, of which credit should be given to the writers for just going with it (a climactic battle that happens while clinging to a ballistic missile in flight?!). However, the dialogue itself is pretty bland and boring, and the sense of humour that they're going for doesn't always hit the mark.

In summary, the JC2 is huge and stunningly beautiful, and the action is ever-present and very fun, which makes this a vast improvement over its predecessor, and lets it stand apart from the other open-world games of its time. In saying that, it lacks the personality of the world that GTA nailed, and the sense of humour that Saints Row did so well, which leaves it feeling comparatively empty at its core. However, if you're looking for spectacle, the game is well-priced and looks amazing, and there's a lot you can do and see in this game that can't be found elsewhere. 

For the price, I highly recommend it.

This open world game was released in 2010. Its size on your disk is around 5 GB. And yet, Just Cause 2 (JC2) is far better than many modern titles which are larger and more complex. The main reason is because it's fun and doesn't hold you back with unnecessary grind. Just Cause 2 is an unapologetically fun experience where you blow up some stuff and then some more.

The best part of all the Just Cause games is their destructive sandbox experience. That is their core strength and the reason why they're so fun. JC2 in particular features over 300 locations including villages, cities, military bases, harbors, offshore rigs, a strip club in the middle of the sky and so on. Each location has vehicle/weapon parts to collect along with destructible elements to (well) destroy. It is this gameplay loop–collect parts, destroy stuff, 100% a location–that makes JC2 so fun and addictive. You can spend hours just doing this.

While Just Cause has been praised for its destructive sandbox experience, the setting itself deserves more appreciation. Just Cause 2 is set in the fictional island country of Panau. Panau is a gorgeous country spanning an area of over 400 square miles. It is full of mountains, plains, rivers, islands etc. and features various climate zones. Once again, I'm amazed by what the devs achieved with just 5 GB for this game!

[h1]Recommendations for Specific Gamers[/h1]

[h2]Mindless Fun[/h2]
Just Cause 2 is mindless fun. You don't have to invest much in the storyline. Perfect game to unwind after work if you enjoy blowing up stuff.

[h2]Achievement Hunters[/h2]
This is a fun game for achievement hunting. No achievement breaking bugs and no need for multiple playthroughs. Slightly grindy to 100%, recommend that you do it in multiple sittings.

[h2]Completionists[/h2]
Absolutely not. Just Cause 2 features hundreds of locations, thousands of collectibles etc. I do not recommend trying to 100% this game.

[h2]East Asian/SE Asian gamers[/h2]
They may (or may not) get offended by the cultural representation of SE Asia in this game. The developers went for a parody of SE Asian culture. This may be amusing to some and not funny to others. At the time Just Cause 2 was released, many Singaporeans loved the bad voice acting in this game. Which is another reason to love JC2.

[h2]Left leaning gamers[/h2]
Just Cause 2 is a smart parody of Western foreign policy and its absurd excesses. Consider this one quote from the game: “Collateral damage is regretted but sanctioned.” The devs knew their political science and inserted it into the game in clever ways. Recommend playing the campaign for the political gags.

[h1]Final Rating[/h1]
8.5/10 (just ‘cause)

A sandbox of chaos, creativity, and unfiltered fun.

Just Cause 2 is a masterclass in open-world mayhem. It doesn’t ask you to take it seriously—in fact, it practically dares you not to. From the moment you step foot on the massive island of Panau, the game hands you a grappling hook, a parachute, and a world begging to be turned upside down.

The strength of Just Cause 2 lies in how it embraces the absurd. The world is enormous, not just in size but in the sheer number of ways you can interact with it. Whether you're hijacking a fighter jet mid-air, tethering enemies to speeding vehicles, or using your grapple-parachute combo to fling yourself across the countryside, every encounter becomes an opportunity for improvisation.

Combat and traversal are tightly linked, giving the game a flow that few open-world titles replicate. You're never limited to the road or the ground, and the movement system makes getting from point A to B genuinely enjoyable. Once you master the rhythm of grappling and gliding, the island becomes your personal playground.

The mission structure might not be the most complex, but that's not what Just Cause 2 is aiming for. The joy comes from how you complete objectives—not the objectives themselves. Blow up a radar station with a stolen tank? Sure. Launch a motorcycle off a cliff into a fuel depot? Even better. The game constantly rewards creativity, and the destructible environments make every mission feel like an explosive set piece waiting to happen.

Visually, the game still holds up remarkably well. The tropical landscapes are vibrant and diverse, from snow-capped peaks to sun-soaked beaches, and the scale of the map remains impressive. The soundtrack and voice acting lean into the campy tone, making the entire experience feel like a high-budget B-action movie—and it’s all the better for it.

For completionists, there's no shortage of content. Between collectibles, side missions, faction tasks, and the simple thrill of wreaking havoc in a variety of vehicles, the hours fly by. And with mods and a passionate fanbase, Just Cause 2 has continued to offer value far beyond its initial release.

In short, Just Cause 2 is the definition of a game that knows exactly what it wants to be: fast, ridiculous, and endlessly entertaining. If you're looking for a break from serious narratives and grounded mechanics, this game offers pure, unfiltered freedom on a cinematic scale.

Coming back to this game after having played the 3rd and 4th installments is truly a breath of fresh air. While Just Cause 3 modernized the series and brought lots of welcome little QoL improvements to the table, Just Cause 4 effectively took the least appealing aspects of JC3 and, rather than dispense with them and mingle the best of 2 and 3, leaned further into them, driving a death nail into the series in the process.

Avalanche went the wrong direction with the series, and it started with the changes to the physics and animation. JC2 is so wonderful for largely the same reason that the violence in Tom and Jerry is wonderful. It's the physics, sound effects, and the sense of real weight and momentum behind everything that makes it so viscerally satisfying and fun. JC3 and, more so, 4 felt very loose and floaty, which immediately breaks immersion.

That was my main gripe with the sequels to this game, but there is a laundry list of other unfortunate design choices that were made that I'm certain others have pointed out.

All that to say, this is the best one.  Absolutely one of the highest value-for-money games you can buy. Most of the time you can buy it for less than a bag of pork rinds. Heck, you can buy this whole series for peanuts. Go ahead. It's not like you can't extract at least [i]some[/i] joy out of JC4. Play it with your friends. Pass the controller around. Get it on your Steam Deck. This series is perfect for mobile.
